definitions.gloss: to appeal to; to make a plea; to call out to
definitions.explanation: To direct an emotional or persuasive message toward someone's feelings, conscience, or reason in order to gain support or sympathy.

examples.japanese: {平和|へいわ}を{訴|うった}えかける。
{彼女|かのじょ}の{言葉|ことば}は{聴衆|ちょうしゅう}の{心|こころ}に{訴|うった}えかけた。
examples.english: Her words appealed to the hearts of the audience.

examples.japanese: {環境|かんきょう}{問題|もんだい}の{深刻|しんこく}さを{市民|しみん}に{訴|うった}えかけるために、{写真展|しゃしんてん}を{開|ひら}いた。
examples.english: We held a photo exhibition to appeal to citizens about the severity of environmental problems.

notes:
Intransitive ichidan compound verb: {訴|うった}え (appeal) + かける (to direct toward). Unlike {訴|うった}える alone, which can mean to sue or complain, {訴|うった}えかける always carries the nuance of an emotional or persuasive appeal.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ～に{訴|うった}えかける (to appeal to someone/something)
- {心|こころ}に{訴|うった}えかける (to touch the heart)
- {感情|かんじょう}に{訴|うった}えかける (to appeal to emotions)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {心|こころ}に{訴|うった}えかける (to tug at the heartstrings)
- {人々|ひとびと}に{訴|うった}えかける (to appeal to people)
- {強|つよ}く{訴|うった}えかける (to make a strong appeal)
